attributes.action: Bring the age down for mammogram
attributes.additional_details:
Many people assume breast cancer only affects older women, but younger adults can and do develop breast cancer. Triple-negative breast cancer, in particular, is often diagnosed at younger ages and can be more aggressive than other types of breast cancer.
This petition is not just about my story. It is about raising awareness that breast cancer does not always wait until age 50. Earlier detection gives people more treatment options, better outcomes, and a greater chance of survival.
attributes.background:
I am starting this petition to call for the age of routine breast cancer screening (mammograms) to be lowered from the current starting age of 50.

I am 33 years old and have recently been diagnosed with triple-negative breast cancer.

rejection.details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could start a new petition clearly stating the age you would like the Government or Parliament to bring the age for routine breast cancer screening down to.

On 29 June 2026, there was a petition debate relating to NHS breast screening. You can find links to read or watch the debate on the relevant petition page: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/742179
